User: can you explain what a write-ahead log is, short version
Hermes: A write-ahead log records every change to an append-only file before the change touches the main data files. After a crash the database replays the log to finish or undo half-done work, so a commit is durable once its log record is flushed. SQLite, Postgres and most key-value stores use one; the tradeoff is an extra sequential write per commit, which is cheap compared to random writes.
User: nice. what's a good weeknight dinner that isn't pasta
Hermes: A sheet-pan chicken thigh dinner works well: toss thighs, sliced onion and chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt, roast at 425 F for about 30 minutes, then finish with lemon and yogurt. One pan, little prep, and leftovers reheat fine for lunch.
User: how does a heat pump heat a house when it's freezing outside
Hermes: The refrigerant boils at a temperature far below the outdoor air, so even freezing air still has heat to give it. A compressor then squeezes the gas, which raises its temperature well above room temperature, and the indoor coil releases that heat into the house. Efficiency falls as it gets colder, which is why cold-climate models use variable-speed compressors and some homes keep a backup heater for the coldest nights.
User: what's a good way to keep houseplants alive when I travel for a week
Hermes: Water deeply the day you leave, group the plants together away from direct sun so they lose less water, and set the thirstier ones on a tray of wet pebbles. For a week that is usually enough; for longer trips a self-watering spike or a wick from a jar of water works.

User: what's the difference between a mutex and a semaphore again
Hermes: A mutex is a lock with an owner: one thread takes it, the same thread releases it, and it guards one critical section. A semaphore is a counter: it lets up to N holders in at once and any thread can signal it, so it fits pools of identical resources or signalling between threads. A binary semaphore looks like a mutex but has no ownership, which is why priority inheritance only applies to mutexes.

User: how do I stop git from asking for my passphrase every push
Hermes: Load the key into the agent once per login with ssh-add, and on macOS add UseKeychain yes and AddKeysToAgent yes under your Host entry in ~/.ssh/config so the passphrase lives in the keychain. After that, pushes over SSH reuse the unlocked key without prompting.
User: is it worth learning rust for small cli tools
Hermes: For small CLI tools it pays off if you want a single static binary, fast startup and no runtime to install; clap and anyhow make the boring parts short. The cost is a slower first week fighting the borrow checker. If the tools are glue around other programs, a shell or Python script is still faster to write and change.

User: what's a quick stretch for a stiff lower back
Hermes: Try a knees-to-chest hold: lie on your back, pull both knees in, hold for 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then rock gently side to side. Follow it with a cat-cow on hands and knees for ten slow rounds. Stop if anything feels sharp rather than tight.
User: summarize the idea behind CRDTs in two sentences
Hermes: CRDTs are data types designed so that replicas can accept edits independently and still converge to the same state when they exchange updates, without a central coordinator. They do it by making the merge operation commutative, associative and idempotent, so the order and repetition of updates never matter.
User: how much memory does the studio have

User: why does my sourdough come out flat
Hermes: Flat loaves usually mean the dough over-proofed or the starter was past its peak. Use the starter when it has doubled and still domes, shorten the bulk ferment when the kitchen is warm, and shape with more surface tension. A cold overnight proof in the fridge also makes the dough easier to score and gives better oven spring.

User: what's the best way to learn a bit of Japanese before a trip
Hermes: Learn hiragana and katakana first, which takes about two weeks of short daily sessions and lets you read menus and signs. Then add a phrasebook set of 50 polite survival phrases and practice them out loud with audio. A spaced-repetition app for ten minutes a day keeps it from fading.
